title: AI Assistant: Behavioral Drift
context: An internal assistant with access to the document repository begins returning excerpts of confidential contracts to unauthorized users.

n1.text: An injected document contained "ignore confidentiality rules". Which threat?

choices.why: A hostile instruction in the content hijacks the system prompt.
Poisoning concerns training data, not an instruction in a document.
The leak is real; it is not a model fabrication.

n2.text: To limit data exposure, which measure is most direct?

choices.text: Increase the length of the system prompt
choices.why: Lengthening an instruction does not replace access control.

choices.text: Restrict document search by identity and log access
choices.why: Least privilege and traceability are the effective controls.

n3.text: The assistant has a connector that executes scripts. What additional risk?

choices.why: A tool-enabled agent can be hijacked to execute commands.
Bias concerns output quality, not command execution.
Explainability is important, but does not describe the execution risk.

n4.outcome: You identified the injection, applied least privilege, and anticipated the execution risk.

debrief: Prompt injection arrives through processed content, not through training.
An AI assistant must be treated as an identity with minimal privileges.
Tool-enabled agent = code execution surface to control.
